name: Herald's Horn
oracle_text:
As this artifact enters, choose a creature type.
Creature spells you cast of the chosen type cost {1} less to cast.
At the beginning of your upkeep, look at the top card of your library. If it's a creature card of the chosen type, you may reveal it and put it into your hand.
blocked_sentences: Creature spells you cast of the chosen type cost {1} less to cast.
At the beginning of your upkeep, look at the top card of your library. If it's a creature card of the chosen type, you may reveal it and put it into your hand.

needs.what: `spell_cost_reduction`'s `affects_spells` filter must accept `{"chosen_type_of": "self"}` in its `subtypes` list, so a cost reduction can be scoped to the type the source permanent named as it entered
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `choose_type` already stores the choice on the permanent and `characteristics.resolve_chosen_subtypes` already substitutes it, but only on the two paths that get handed the source permanent: static `affects` (via `characteristics._matches`) and trigger filters (via `triggers`). `spell_cost_reduction` prices a card still in hand through `characteristics._matches_printed(card, filt)`, which takes no source object at all and so has nothing to read `chosen_type` off; the literal dict then reaches `set(subtypes)` and is unhashable. A literal subtype list cannot stand in either, because the type is not known until the artifact enters.

needs.what: the effect-side selector language (`effects.selectors.matches`, used by `look_at_top`'s `objects`) must accept `{"chosen_type_of": "self"}` in `subtypes`, so an ability can ask "is this a creature card of the chosen type" about a card in a library
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `resolve_chosen_subtypes` is never called from `effects/selectors.py`; its `subtypes` branch does a plain `set(want) & subtypes`, so the marker dict raises rather than resolving. The trigger-filter path does resolve it, but the printed line triggers on `upkeep`, which binds no object to filter, so the test has to happen inside the effect on the library's top card. `look_at_top` with `count: "any"` is otherwise the exact shape of "look at the top card... you may... put it into your hand".
